---
title: "8. Vertical and sexual transmission: when K has no closed form but K_S does"
subtitle: "ReproductiveNumbers.jl vignettes"
author: "Simon D. W. Frost"
date: today
---

## Overview

Section 4.2 of Diekmann, Heesterbeek and Roberts (2010) considers a sexually transmitted
infection in which infected adults of either sex also bear infected juveniles. There are
four infected states (juvenile and adult, female and male) and all four are
states-at-infection, so `K` is `4 × 4`. Its irreducible part is `3 × 3`, which has no
closed-form dominant eigenvalue. But `T` has rank two, because only the two *adult* states
transmit, and the small-domain matrix `K_S = -RΣ⁻¹C` of section 3.3 is `2 × 2`. The package
falls back to `K_S` automatically.

The paper only gives the linearised infected subsystem; the full model below is one
consistent choice (susceptible adults are born at rate `μ`, minus the infected births).

## The model

```{julia}
using ReproductiveNumbers, ModelingToolkit, Symbolics, LinearAlgebra
using ModelingToolkit: t_nounits as t, D_nounits as D

@parameters p μ ν₁ ν₂ γ₁ γ₂ β₁ β₂ N₁ N₂
@variables S₁(t) J₁(t) I₁(t) S₂(t) J₂(t) I₂(t)
eqs = [D(S₁) ~ μ * N₁ - p * μ * I₁ - β₁ * S₁ * I₂ / N₂ - μ * S₁,
    D(J₁) ~ p * μ * I₁ - (ν₁ + μ) * J₁,
    D(I₁) ~ ν₁ * J₁ + β₁ * S₁ * I₂ / N₂ - (γ₁ + μ) * I₁,
    D(S₂) ~ μ * N₂ - p * μ * I₂ - β₂ * S₂ * I₁ / N₁ - μ * S₂,
    D(J₂) ~ p * μ * I₂ - (ν₂ + μ) * J₂,
    D(I₂) ~ ν₂ * J₂ + β₂ * S₂ * I₁ / N₁ - (γ₂ + μ) * I₂]
sti = complete(System(eqs, t; name = :sti_vertical))
```

Vertical transmission `p μ Iᵢ` is linear in the infected states, so the default rule
would file it as a transition (see the guide on choosing transmissions). We give the
new-infection rates explicitly:

```{julia}
ngm = next_generation_matrix(sti, [J₁, I₁, J₂, I₂];
    transmission = [p * μ * I₁, β₁ * S₁ * I₂ / N₂,
        p * μ * I₂, β₂ * S₂ * I₁ / N₁])
```

## K is singular

```{julia}
ngm.K
```

```{julia}
symbolic_isequal(det(ngm.K), 0), irreducible_blocks(ngm.K)
```

The `3 × 3` block has rank two, so `spectral_radius` alone cannot give a closed form:

```{julia}
try
    spectral_radius(ngm.K)
catch err
    err
end
```

## The small domain

```{julia}
K_S = small_domain_matrix(ngm)
```

`K_S` counts generations of *infectious adults*: its diagonal entries are the expected
number of infectious adults of the same sex produced through vertical transmission (an
infected juvenile must survive to maturity, `νᵢ/(νᵢ + μ)`), and its off-diagonal entries
the sexual transmissions. `basic_reproduction_number` uses it automatically:

```{julia}
R0 = basic_reproduction_number(ngm)
```

```{julia}
vals = Dict(p => 0.3, μ => 0.02, ν₁ => 0.1, ν₂ => 0.1, γ₁ => 0.2, γ₂ => 0.25,
    β₁ => 0.4, β₂ => 0.5, N₁ => 1000.0, N₂ => 1000.0)
num = evaluate(ngm, vals)
(basic_reproduction_number(num), ReproductiveNumbers.to_number(substitute(R0, vals)))
```

The non-zero spectra of `K` and `K_S` coincide:

```{julia}
nz(A) = sort(abs.(filter(x -> abs(x) > 1e-9, eigvals(A))))
nz(num.K), nz(ReproductiveNumbers.to_number.(substitute.(K_S, Ref(vals))))
```

## Which parameters matter most?

```{julia}
elasticities(ngm, vals; params = [p, β₁, β₂, ν₁, γ₁])
```
